title: The Blind Men in the City of Agra (HI)
summary: Akbar claims blind men are rare in Agra. Birbal sits on the street mending a shoe and proves that the blind outnumber the sighted ten to one.
full_text:
While discussing the imperial charitable pensions for the disabled, Emperor Akbar remarked: 'Fortunately, blindness is rare in our capital. My census records barely two hundred blind persons in all of Agra.'

Birbal smiled: 'Sire, your census records only those whose physical eyes are damaged. But the number of people who have eyes and yet walk through life completely blind to what is directly in front of them is thousands of times greater!'

Akbar scoffed: 'Nonsense, Birbal! Prove that the blind outnumber the sighted, or withdraw your claim!'

The next morning, Birbal went to the busiest crossroads near the Agra bazaar. He placed a wooden stool on the street, took out a cobbler's awl, a strip of leather, and an old slipper, and began vigorously mending the shoe. Beside him sat a scribe with a large scroll and an inkpot.

Presently, an imperial nobleman rode by on his horse. Seeing the grand minister sitting in the dust, the nobleman stopped and asked in astonishment: 'Raja Birbal! What on earth are you doing?'

Birbal did not answer; he simply said to his scribe: 'Write down his name.'

A merchant passed by: 'Raja Birbal! Are you mending a shoe?'

'Write down his name,' Birbal instructed the scribe.

Throughout the day, hundreds of courtiers, guards, merchants, and citizens stopped at the crossroads, looked directly at Birbal holding a needle and leather, and asked: 'Birbal, are you mending a shoe?'

Every time, Birbal had the scribe record the person's name on the scroll.

By late afternoon, Emperor Akbar himself rode by with his retinue. Seeing his chief minister sitting in the street with a cobbler's awl, Akbar stopped his horse and exclaimed: 'Birbal! What are you doing? Are you mending a shoe?'

Birbal smiled, stood up, and said to his scribe: 'Write down Emperor Akbar's name at the very top of the list!'

Akbar was indignant: 'Why did you add my name to that list? What list is that?'

Birbal handed the long scroll to the Emperor:

'Sire, this is the official census of the blind men of Agra! Every person on this list saw me sitting here in plain daylight with an awl, leather, and a needle, and yet asked me what I was doing! If their eyes were truly functioning, they would have seen the obvious without needing to ask!

'And with deepest respect, Your Majesty is the king of the blind, for you saw the shoe in my hand and asked the very same question!'

Akbar stared in disbelief, then burst into a roar of laughter, acknowledging that seeing is an act of the mind, not merely the eyes.
